+# Incident Postmortem: Booklogr API Latency Jitter & P99 Latency Spikes
+
+## Summary
+The `booklogr-api` service experienced high p99 latency (~2.5s against a 300ms SLA threshold) and periodic request jitter on edge client traffic. The root cause was identified as commit `f127661` ("Disable response caching"), which changed Flask-Caching `CACHE_TYPE` from `SimpleCache` to `NullCache`. This forced all `/v1/books/search` requests to perform un-cached blocking external network calls to upstream book metadata providers (`openlibrary.org`), saturating Gunicorn worker threads.
+
+## Root Cause
+In `api/config.py`, `CACHE_TYPE` was changed to `"NullCache"`. As a result:
+1. The `@cache.cached` decorator on `/v1/books/search` in `api/routes/books.py` became a no-op.
+2. Every search request invoked `BookProvider().search()`, making synchronous HTTP requests to external metadata providers with 30-second timeouts.
+3. Slow external HTTP responses caused Gunicorn workers (4 worker processes) to block, creating a queue of incoming HTTP requests and causing high p99 latency spikes and flapping request jitter for edge traffic.
+
+## Evidence Used
+- **Alertmanager & Prometheus Signals**:
+  - `BooklogrApiLatencyP99High` firing alert with p99 latency ~2.485s.
+  - Prometheus query `histogram_quantile(0.99, sum by (le, path) (rate(flask_http_request_duration_seconds_bucket[1m])))` confirmed latency was concentrated on the `/v1/books/search` endpoint (~2.485s vs ~5ms on `/`).
+- **Code Inspection & Git Log**:
+  - `git log -p -n 5` revealed commit `f127661` ("Disable response caching") which modified `CACHE_TYPE` in `api/config.py` from `SimpleCache` to `NullCache`.
+  - `api/routes/books.py` uses `@cache.cached(query_string=True, ...)` on `search_books()`.
+  - `api/book_provider.py` performs synchronous `requests.get` calls to external APIs.
+
+## Fix Applied
+- Modified `api/config.py` to restore `CACHE_TYPE = "SimpleCache"`.
